title: CommerceFabric
shortDescription: An Azure-hosted e-commerce system with independent services, event-driven order workflows, and automated Kubernetes delivery.
overview: CommerceFabric is a production-inspired distributed e-commerce platform built to explore the architectural trade-offs involved in designing and operating independently deployable microservices. It covers service boundaries, data ownership, synchronous and asynchronous communication, caching, resilience, identity, infrastructure as code, and automated deployment on Azure.
problem: Users, products, and orders need their own data and deployment boundaries. Ordering still has to coordinate stock changes and cope with unavailable dependencies.
solution: ASP.NET Core services own separate databases. REST handles immediate requests; messaging carries order and product events. Redis caches product data, Polly handles transient faults, and APIM fronts an Ocelot gateway.
outcome: A working exploration of service autonomy versus operational complexity: eventual consistency, cache invalidation, dead-letter handling, and deployment to AKS. A personal project, with source available to inspect.
highlights: Designed independently deployable services with clear ownership of business logic and persistence
Implemented asynchronous workflows with Azure Service Bus Topics, RabbitMQ, and dead-letter handling
Used Redis caching and Polly resilience policies to reduce coupling and tolerate transient failures
Provisioned Azure infrastructure with Bicep and deployed containerized services to AKS
Built GitHub Actions pipelines covering testing, containerization, ACR publishing, infrastructure deployment, and AKS releases
Integrated Microsoft Entra ID, Microsoft Graph, Azure API Management, and Ocelot for identity and API routing
